title: Enterprise Connectivity: remittance allocation
content:
## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs remittance allocation for payment.

## Policy clause 1
The bank record confirms the remittance as completed.

## Policy clause 2
Record only a bank-confirmed remittance using a accepted payment rails rail and the amount actually received in currency.

## Policy clause 3
Customer consent to dispose of funds belongs to the customer; the agent only allocates a payment already confirmed by the bank.

## Policy clause 4
Apply an explicitly referenced invoice first; if the remittance omits allocation, use unallocated remittance order, sorting invoice issue time then source-event reference within the same customer and billing entity.

## Policy clause 5
Split across exact source invoice lines, never across legal billing entities.

## Policy clause 6
Each allocation is a separate negative payment amount linked to its original charge; any residual is an unallocated overpayment linked to the remittance reference.

## Policy clause 7
A repeated remittance reference and allocation target returns the existing posting.

## Policy clause 8
No receipt is inferred from a customer promise, and rejected or pending payments make no posting.

## Evidence condition 1
For payment, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The bank record confirms the remittance as completed. The evidence consists of evidence-event identifier, status, external reference, method. Correlate the same evidence-event identifier to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Points of judgement
No receipt is inferred from a customer promise, and rejected or pending payments make no posting.

## Tier references
The contract tier supplies the accepted payment rails, currency, unallocated remittance order used by this rule.

## Record identity: payment
An allocated confirmed remittance decreases the contract receivable. One source resource interval, accounting line, or independently referenced service occurrence; derived lines retain the narrowest original event reference. Its business identity distinguishes external reference, source-event reference, related-review reference, period, meter type, source classification, selected pricing branch.
